transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Gritty residue on dishes is very common and usually comes from a blocked filter, restricted spray jets, or hard water issues rather than a broken part. Let's check the basics first. Please switch off and unplug the dishwasher. Take out the bottom rack and twist the filter assembly in the base of the tub to remove it. Also, spin the spray arms by hand; do they turn freely, or are the little jet holes blocked?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok done that. filter was full of food n grease, gross. upper spray arm is a bit stiff but lower one spins fine. there is a musty smell too

[Heading: Blocked or stiff upper spray arm/jets]
That explains the gritty bits – food trapped in the filter gets recirculated and lands on your dishes as grit. The musty smell is likely from that same trapped debris. Since the upper arm was stiff, it’s probably not spinning properly during the wash cycle, which means water isn't reaching the top rack effectively. Please remove the upper spray arm (it usually lifts off or unscrews) and check for grit in the jets. Clean them with an old toothbrush or a pin, and also clean the spindle/bearing where it mounts to clear that stiffness. Once cleaned, does it spin freely by hand?
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok took the upper arm off, several holes were blocked with seeds n limescale. cleared them with a cocktail stick n its spinning better now

[Heading: Blocked spray arm jets and dirty filter causing poor water distribution]
That sounds like exactly what was causing the problem – seeds and limescale in the jets would stop water from reaching your top rack properly, and a dirty filter recirculates grit. If they're still gritty or if you notice a white chalky film instead, let me know; that would point to hard water settings needing adjustment rather than a mechanical fault.
